3526.d:
A polyline of four segments rotates around a moving center, progressively changing its configuration. The center of rotation moves from a random point at the top left and descends following a serpentine path. The changes are made by rotating the first segment around the center and subsequent segments around the end vertex of the previous one. A new polyline is added at each frame, and all others are shifted along the path.

The lengths of the four segments and their rotation speeds are defined randomly at the beginning and are different for each mint. 

The color palettes are defined algorithmically from the randomly chosen background color. The colors of the polylines are then derived from the opposite ones in the color wheel, lightening the initial ones to white and darkening the final ones.

Antonio Belluscio (@livinbits)
December 2021

Through a click or tap, you can jump to a different moment in the virtually infinite evolution of the waves.

3560.d:
A colorful simulation of the physarum polycephalum. A slime mold. 

Each slime cell is represented by a pixel. Every iteration a slime samples the area to the front, front-left and front-right. Depending on the color value of each sample it will decide whether to turn left, turn right or move straight ahead. These simple rules cause the slimes to form these organic looking patterns. 

The values for the sense directions, sense distance, turn angle and movement speed are different for each color.

Depending on the hash, the different colors also have a chance to be "infectious", causing other slime to turn to their color if they touch. (Red eats green, green eats blue, blue eats red).

Many thanks to these two resources from which I learned about this interesting slime :) 
https://www.sagejenson.com/physarum
https://github.com/nicoptere/physarum

Created with Three.js

Human feature detection theory proposes that the human nervous system sorts and
filters incoming stimuli to allow a human to make sense of visual information,
though it might be just random visual appearances.

This series takes inspiration from the psychological Rorschachtest introduced
by Swiss psychologist Hermann Rorschach. Each token features a generative system

This series pays homage to Dennis Ritchie.
P5.js is a very beginner friendly programming environment, as I can attest from my own experience. The first programming language I learned was C, and then VB, JAVA, Android and so on. P5.js is arguably the easiest programming language to get started with that I've seen so far. While you're learning p5.js, you'll also be able to learn JavaScript to render creative, interesting things on any browser. Of course, you can also use it to do a lot of things, do art creation, data visualization, interactive art and so on.
Here I want to break the traditional concept and use my own unique method to paint, to show the unique charm of our team.
I added a random element to it, so that each of them was randomly generated.
CTRL + S saves the work to the desktop.

3610.d:
Mei(梅):

"Mei" is an oriental art piece featuring the imagery of plum blossom, a symbol of courage and perseverance in traditional Chinese culture.

The generative system at the backend of "Mei" is an exploration of this cultural symbol by modern art language. The basic elements of the paintings are merely circles and enclosed flow field shapes. A great variety of short and light strokes of such elements are used across the paintings. Xuan paper is occasionally used as background, which is a painting material since the Tang dynasty.

Mei's outputs span different stages of plum blossom from winter to spring. The scene also changes from a calm day to snowy or even stormy weather. The consistent yet complex senses and feelings reflected are surprisingly versatile.

3622.d:
The third piece in this series is dedicated to another fundamental algorithm in computer graphics: Voronoi. It's origin precedes its use with computers by several decades, or centuries, depending on who to credit, since science always is a continuum. In the generative art & design field, the algorithm has been an instrumental tool for generation(s) of practioners, sadly often to the point of turning cliché.

In this piece I've attempted to "break" the classic resulting aesthetics of this algorithm and focus more on revealing its inner workings. There are many ways of computing a Voronoi diagram. The so called Jump Flood Algorithm (JFA) proved to be the visually most interesting approach to me. Again, as with the previous De/Frag piece, here the algorithm has been slowed down, timesliced and customized in dozens of ways to result in a more painterly character overall and produce a variety of new shapes & textures.

Fullscreen compatible (Press 'S' to toggle square frame). Made with love & thi.ng/umbrella

3627.d:
When the Impressionists first exhibited their work, they derided as lunatics by the art establishment. The vitriol then -- "wallpaper in its embryonic state is more finished than that seascape" (referring to Impression: sunrise by Monet) -- reminds me of criticism that generative art, and the NFT world more generally, are subject to now. "Impossible cathedrals" is a tribute to rebels who dare to see the world differently. 

Since generative art is often criticized as cold and austere, I took this as a challenge to reproduce the spirit of impressionism. Impossible cathedrals -- interwoven arches that cannot exist in reality -- hint at some of the favorite subjects of the impressionists.

The title alludes to Italo Calvino's novel Invisible Cities, a rebel in another context. Other artists who I had in mind during creation: the Japanese woodblock printing artists Kawase Hasui and Hiroshi Yoshida; American painter JAM Whistler.

Impossible cathedrals was written in p5.js using elements of code by eeedg (thanks)

This is a series of collages produced generatively; each from a spread of pictures derived and painted over from a screenshot from “Tanin no kao”; a beautiful Japanese classic film written by Kôbô Abe and directed by Hiroshi Teshigahara. In the film; Mr Okuyama (portreyed by Tatsuya Nakadai) wears this mask/face of the man with with a mole (played by Hisashi Igawa) in an effort to seduce his own wife as someone else.

“The face is just a few dozen square inches above the neck, covered with a layer of dough. Isn't that right? I wanted to think so. I told myself a million times it was only a layer of skin, a surface. But now I'm not so sure. The face is the door to the soul. When the face is closed off, so too is the soul. Nobody is allowed inside. The soul is left to rot, reduced to ruins. It becomes the soul of a monster, rotten to the core. I feel as if I've been buried alive.”

The third piece in this series is dedicated to another fundamental algorithm in computer graphics: Voronoi. It's origin precedes its use with computers by several decades, or centuries, depending on who to credit, since science always is a continuum. In the generative art & design field, the algorithm has been an instrumental tool for generation(s) of practioners, sadly often to the point of turning cliché.

In this piece I've attempted to "break" the classic resulting aesthetics of this algorithm and focus more on revealing its inner workings. There are many ways of computing a Voronoi diagram. The so called Jump Flood Algorithm (JFA) proved to be the visually most interesting approach to me. Again, as with the previous De/Frag piece, here the algorithm has been slowed down, timesliced and customized in dozens of ways to result in a more painterly character overall and produce a variety of new shapes & textures.

Fullscreen compatible (Press 'S' to toggle square frame). Made with love & thi.ng/umbrella

3631.d:
I have long meant to do a piece inspired by the covers of the famous (to the sort of people that like Dutch electronic music from the 1950s) Philips "Popular Electronics" 7" records. Yesterday I finally sat down and did one. "intersection" takes as its source material the cover art of the first record in the set, "Electronic Music," which is a split single by Tom Dissevelt and Kid Battan. You can listen to it on YouTube if you are curious. (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z6T-jZUHcI8 and it's a banger!)

Rather than recreating the cover art directly, I just briefly looked at it (I have the real vinyl records, because I'm the sort of person that has strange things like that) to wedge it in my brain, and then didn't look at it again. As a result, my piece has the "feel" of the record cover, but doesn't actually look like it at all. This is a satisfying result for me. 

Created in p5.js.

Candy coloured infinity ribbons play out an elaborate looped dance. Some loops take time to develop, you can skip through the performance by pressing the space bar.
There are 6 delicious candied colour schemes (and a secret one) and a whole bunch of other features that make your mint unique...

'growthPhase' determines how long the ribbons take to grow and shrink in length.
'cyclePhase' determines how long a full looped arrangement lasts.

At the slowest rate your performance will take 17 minutes to complete, the fastest is 34 seconds.

I understand that not everyone has 17 minutes spare to gaze at some artwork. You can press the space bar to jump 200 frames, this way you can very quickly scan through your loop to see how it unfolds. If you are having performance issue you can also press the + or - keys to increase or reduce tessellation.

SPACE - Skip 200 Frames
+ / - Increase or decrease ribbon tessellation (between 5 and 200 verts per edge)

- General color palette
- Landscape seed
- Water amount (you can get archipelagos or vast landscapes)
- Camera position

3663.d:
This piece can be thought as a reflection on the paths we follow while finding our way through life.

Some of us explore more paths, others, less. Often, we find ourselves where we had been before, and we have to start again. Sometimes we take bold steps, sometimes less bold ones. Some paths are filled with love, others, with blues. 
We grow up, and we broaden our paths, or narrow them. 

Or, you can think of this piece as just a bunch of lines, grown progressively using a process similar to Substrate (Jared Tarbell, 2003), modified with a vector field generated with trigonometric functions. 

Random features include the color palette, the number of lines, their width, the scaling of the vector field, and margins.

Some color palettes were inspired by the beautiful plotter works of Iskra Velitchkova.

Original artwork by Roberto Ranon aka Dobleganger aka Doble · Made with p5.js · Udine, 2021

The appearance of any textile is mainly based on its weaving pattern. Since warp yarns (the lengthwise threads in a roll) are usually covered by filling yarns, the underlying pattern is not visible. By increasing the size of threads, i.e. using ribbons or belts instead of thin threads, these intricate, almost microscopic structures are revealed.

This series is a collaboration with my Mum Pia. Each Woven Pattern of the diagonal series is generated by using random diagonal fill rules on a 6x6 rapport.

My mum's work explores and emphasises the aesthetic of these classic, yet complex structures by magnifying them for the viewer. 3676.c:
The appearance of any textile is mainly based on its weaving pattern. Since warp yarns (the lengthwise threads in a roll) are usually covered by filling yarns, the underlying pattern is not visible. By increasing the size of threads, i.e. using ribbons or belts instead of thin threads, these intricate, almost microscopic structures are revealed.

This series is a collaboration with my Mum Pia. Each Woven Pattern of the diagonal series is generated by using random diagonal fill rules on a 6x6 rapport.

This is a facade. This is movement through many dimensions simultaneously, crushed into this frame, together, and expressed as X, Y, and C position (position along a 4-bit color scale). Each frame is created by analyzing the contents of the previous frame. As these cascade events play out, I reflect pieces of the display through grids spanning the screen, and again reflect everything 4 ways. This irreversibly corrupts the relationship that existed between the visualized pattern, and the “real” pattern. Corrupts, but doesn’t destroy. The brain believes it sees the pattern... who can say for sure? Nothing can be confirmed beyond the wall of Entropy this process presents. This is what it means to be irreversible.

23 palettes -> 15 (6%), 4 (1.75%), 4 1-bit (0.75%)
mirror types -> double (95%), vert (2%), hor (2%), none (1%)
and other rare features!

Wabi-sabi (侘寂): appreciate impermanence and imperfection

There is little chance of a 'perfect' work of art. The small imperfections require reflection. 

The variation and randomness give the work some asymmetry, common in wabi-sabi esthetics. Because of a limited color palette and the simple shapes used, the works keep their simplicity (another principle of wabi-sabi). The noisy texture gives it some roughness, indeed again a core principle of wabi-sabi. 

The colors are reminiscent of the 70s and 80s. Some think that everything was better in the past. The trick is to enjoy the moment.

Thinking about impermanence is sometimes uncomfortable, 'ongemak' in Dutch, but also valuable.

In truth -- it is only an abstract kinetic sculpture, a play of light
and shadow, but some viewers may find themselves transported to that
beautiful river scene, where the morning light reaches into the winding valley....

December 2021

3696.d:
Uninhabitable is a generative system built only from ellipses. The process of playing with different geometric and trigonometric disruptions gives rise to four different compositions which seek to evoque living constructions and environments. Besides the shape itself and its related distortion, the stroke weight of the lines plays a meaningful role in the piece. Following a discrete range [0.01,0.1,1] the weight reveals the process allowing the viewer to realize the trace of the huge amount of lines in each piece. This back and forth between scales and context is, while kind of stripping the code, part of my continuing interest on understanding the -usually- crazy paths of machines' way of thinking.

Press "h" to see it and high resolution and refresh to get back to the initial state. Press "h" to save it.

Uninhabitable is an original work by Iskra Velitchkova. 2021.

3729.d:
The third piece in this series is dedicated to another fundamental algorithm in computer graphics: Voronoi. It's origin precedes its use with computers by several decades, or centuries, depending on who to credit, since science always is a continuum. In the generative art & design field, the algorithm has been an instrumental tool for generation(s) of practioners, sadly often to the point of turning cliché.

In this piece I've attempted to "break" the classic resulting aesthetics of this algorithm and focus more on revealing its inner workings. There are many ways of computing a Voronoi diagram. The so called Jump Flood Algorithm (JFA) proved to be the visually most interesting approach to me. Again, as with the previous De/Frag piece, here the algorithm has been slowed down, timesliced and customized in dozens of ways to result in a more painterly character overall and produce a variety of new shapes & textures.

Fullscreen compatible (Press 'S' to toggle square frame). Made with love & thi.ng/umbrella

"Garden, " is the result of an algorithm that started in April 2021. It was called "Grass.js".
Spring was blooming all around the house, taking over the stones and remnants of ancient battles that stood here. Inspiration was everywhere.
The initial goal was to use mathematical formulas for creating patterns inspired by the density of nature, that could be used by a pen plotter, so it kept focusing on outputting vector lines. This history and practice produced a graphical style based on line strokes, plus occasionally some transparent, filled shapes.

at a drafting table, straight edge in hand, imagining what might be possible.

3743.d:
Parhun is our first generative piece. It uses handcrafted tiles paired 
with generative programming. Inspired by the Middle East's unique shapes and patterns 
like stars on the Persian kilims and the shape of the monument Domes combined with 
geometric shapes. It reflects the unique and complex nature of our home.

Every buyer gets 5 out of more than 30 carefully curated color palettes and an 
exhaustive amount of tile combinations bound to some unique property combinations.

Every piece is a generated SVG and can be printed in any size.

Click / Space Key -> New grid / palette

Ctrl / Cmd + P -> Print
